'''Leena Peltonen-Palotie''' (16 June 1952 &ndash; 11 March 2010)<ref name="aka.fi_20100311">{{Cite web |url= http://www.aka.fi/en-gb/A/Academy-of-Finland/The-Academy/Releases/Obituary-Professor-Leena-Peltonen-Palotie-Academician-of-Science/ |title= Obituary: Professor Leena Peltonen-Palotie, Academician of Science |access-date= 11 March 2010 |date= 11 March 2010 |publisher= Academy of Finland |location= Helsinki |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100316083840/http://www.aka.fi/en-gb/A/Academy-of-Finland/The-Academy/Releases/Obituary-Professor-Leena-Peltonen-Palotie-Academician-of-Science/ |archive-date= 16 March 2010 }}</ref> was a Finnish [[geneticist]] who contributed to the identification of 15 genes for [[Finnish heritage disease]]s, including [[arterial hypertension]], [[schizophrenia]], [[lactose intolerance]], [[arthrosis]] and [[multiple sclerosis]]. She was considered one of the world's leading molecular geneticists.<ref name="aka.fi_20100311" /><ref name="hs.fi_20100311" />

==Biography==
Peltonen-Palotie was born in [[Helsinki]], but her family moved to [[Oulu]] when she was five years old. She completed her secondary education at the [[Oulun Suomalaisen Yhteiskoulun Lukio|Finnish Co-educational Lycée of Oulu]], graduating in 1971. Peltonen-Palotie went on to study medicine, receiving her [[Licentiate (degree)#Finland and Sweden|Licentiate]] of Medicine degree in 1976, and completed her [[Doctor (title)#Finland|doctoral]] thesis at the [[University of Oulu]] in 1978.<ref name="Kaleva_2009">{{Cite web |last=Mar 2010 |first= |title=Professor Leena Peltonen-Palotie: 1952-2010 |url=https://www.sanger.ac.uk/news_item/2010-03-11-professor-leena-peltonen-palotie-1952-2010/ |access-date=2024-03-13 |website=Wellcome Sanger Institute |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Peltonen-Palotie worked at the [[National Public Health Institute of Finland]] from 1987 to 1998. From 1998 to 2002 she helped found the [[UCLA]] Department of Human Genetics.<ref>{{Cite web| url=http://www.genetics.ucla.edu/leena.html| title=In Memoriam: Leena Peltonen| access-date=17 November 2010| url-status=dead| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100708110110/http://www.genetics.ucla.edu/leena.html| archive-date=8 July 2010}}</ref> She had a professorial position in the [[Academy of Finland]] since 2003. In April 2005 Peltonen-Palotie was employed at the [[University of Helsinki]] and the National Public Health Institute of Finland. She was also the project director for the [[EU]] project GenomEUtwin that was formed to define and characterize the genetic components in the background of different diseases. In 2004 she became a member of the Board of Directors of [[Orion Corporation (pharmaceutical company)|Orion Corporation]], the largest Finnish pharmaceutical company. In September 2007, Peltonen-Palotie joined the [[Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute]] as the head of Human Genetics. She also headed research groups at the [[Broad Institute]] of [[MIT]] and [[Harvard University]].<ref name="hs.fi_20100311">{{Cite web |url= http://www.hs.fi/english/article/Leena+Peltonen-Palotie+1952-2010/1135253737850 |title= Leena Peltonen-Palotie (1952–2010) – Internationally renowned geneticist dies at 57 |access-date= 11 March 2010 |date= 11 March 2010 |publisher= [[Helsingin Sanomat]] |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100314161449/http://www.hs.fi/english/article/Leena+Peltonen-Palotie+1952-2010/1135253737850 |archive-date= 14 March 2010 }}</ref>

Peltonen-Palotie published over 500 research articles and almost 80 invited articles,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015 |title=THE WORLD'S MOST INFLUENTIAL SCIENTIFIC MINDS |url=https://www.ludwigcancerresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/37a987a9-e378-4888-8baa-d4ba20efdbfd_tr_scientific_minds_online_final.pdf |website=Ludwig Cancer Research |publisher=Thomson Reuters}}</ref> and mentored over 70 [[PhD student]]s in her career.<ref name="hs.fi_20100311"/>

She died on 11 March 2010<ref name="aka.fi_20100311" /> at age 57 from [[bone cancer]].<ref name="kuolinsyy">{{Cite web |url= http://www.iltasanomat.fi/uutiset/kotimaa/uutinen.asp?id=2033971&ref=lk_hs_ko_2 |archive-url= https://archive.today/20130106191525/http://www.iltasanomat.fi/uutiset/kotimaa/uutinen.asp?id=2033971&ref=lk_hs_ko_2 |url-status= dead |archive-date= 6 January 2013 |title= Leena Palotie kuoli syöpään |access-date=11 March 2010 |date= 11 March 2010 |publisher= Ilta-Sanomat |language=fi}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
* In addition to many academic awards she received an [[honorary degree]] from the Faculty of Medicine at [[University of Uppsala]] in 2000,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/honorary-doctorates/medicine/ |title =Honorary Doctors of the Faculty of Medicine |work= Uppsala University, Sweden |access-date=11 May 2023}}</ref> {{clarify span|text=and the [[University of Joensuu]].|date=December 2019}} 
* In 2004, the Finnish television show {{Lang|fi|[[Suuret suomalaiset]]}} listed Peltonen-Palotie as 77th of the 100 greatest Finns of all time. 
* In 2006, Peltonen-Palotie was awarded the Belgian {{Lang|nl|Prix van Gysel}} and the Swedish {{Lang|sv|Stora Fernströmpriset}} prizes. In 2009, she was awarded the Finnish honorary title of [[Academician#Finland|Academician of Science]].<ref name="aka.fi_20100311" />
* On [[International Women's Day]] 2010, her achievements were honored in the form of a commemorative [[postage stamp]] issued by the Finnish Post.<ref name="hs.fi_20100311"/>
* The Leena Peltonen Prize for Excellence in Human Genetics is named in her honor.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fimm.fi/en/news/1504594931|title=Leena Peltonen (Palotie) prize 2018 – Call for submission of candidates |last=mari.kaunisto |date=2017-09-05 |website=FIMM |language=en |access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref>
